subject: MAP: unitized cost-trace validation + evaluation plan (tokens/$, caching & batching)
messages:

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff questions — tokens/$ clarity

Irene / team — thanks again for the demo last week. Before we sign the MAP we need a short technical validation that the cost assumptions in your proposal match our traffic patterns. Two specific asks from finance and infra: 

1) A reproducible trace (CSV) showing tokens-per-request distribution for our pilot traffic (we attached a sample slice).
2) Clear assumptions for cache hit rates and batching windows used to derive tokens/$ in the SOW.

We'd like to validate a 48-hour synthetic run on our staging dataset and review the output (tokens consumed, latency, and cost delta vs the quoted unit price). Can you confirm you can produce that trace and a short runbook for how you'll simulate prefetch/cache behavior?

Amit
Head of Platform Engineering
Novus Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP: unitized cost-trace validation + evaluation plan (tokens/$, caching & batching)

Amit — thanks for the clear asks. We can absolutely run a 48-hour evaluation and provide a reproducible trace and the runbook. High-level answer first, then a proposed schedule and owners.

Quick summary of assumptions we'll validate (we'll include these in the MAP appendix):
- tokens per API call: we'll use your sample slice to derive the empirical prompt + response token distribution and table the median / 95th percentiles.
- cache model: two modes — (A) prefix KV-cache with nominal hit rates (we'll test 10%, 30%, 60%); (B) session-level streaming caches (simulated TTLs 30s / 5m).
- batching behavior: continuous batching with target latency windows 20ms / 100ms / 500ms to show cost vs p95 latency tradeoffs.
- fallbacks: if the primary 8-bit quantized variant increases error beyond your eval thresholds, we will auto-fallback to the 16-bit variant — we will measure token delta and per-token price delta for both.

Proposed evaluation plan and timeline: 
- Nov 19: Redwood to produce a sanitized trace (MAP-traffic-samples.csv) and a short runbook (unit-cost-simulation-notes.pdf). 
- Nov 20–21: Redwood runs parameter sweep (cache hit rates x batching windows x model variants) on a replicated staging environment for 48h.
- Nov 22: Internal analysis, create MAP-responsibility-grid.xlsx with owners, and assemble a 1-page unit-econ summary.
- Nov 23: Joint readout with Novus (30–45 min) to review tokens/$ sensitivity and acceptance criteria.

Owners: Irene — lead readout, Karthik — simulation engineer (executes sweep & collects traces), Marissa — unit-econ analyst (prepare the summary and delta table).

I'll drop the first trace and the runbook to the shared Drive link and attach the CSV here. Let us know if those timeline dates are tight for you.

Thanks,
Irene Choi

irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Amit Patel <amit.patel@novushealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: unitized cost-trace validation + evaluation plan (tokens/$, caching & batching)

Looping in execution details so the simulation is reproducible on both sides. Quoting Irene's plan below and adding concrete steps we will run and the exact outputs we'll deliver.

Execution steps (Karthik / Redwood infra):
- Step 0: Sanitize the sample slice to remove PII and split by endpoint. Output: MAP-traffic-samples.csv (columns: request_id, endpoint, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id, timestamp).
- Step 1: Replay engine: we will replay at your requested ingest rates (we'll start at pilot baseline of 12 rps, ramp to 100 rps). Each replay run will produce a per-request token tally and latencies.
- Step 2: Cache simulation: three profiles (low/med/high) with a deterministic hit-rate injection layer so results are comparable. We'll tag each request with cache_hit = true/false in the output trace.
- Step 3: Batching profiles: three windows — 20ms, 100ms, 500ms. For each request we log batch_size and batching_delay_ms.
- Step 4: Model variants: q8 (8-bit) and fp16 baseline. For each variant we record per-token cost multiplier (e.g., q8 = 0.75x per-token compute cost) and a quality delta field (response_qa_delta).
- Step 5: Aggregation: produce the following artifacts:
  * per_run_token_summary.csv (tokens_total, avg_tokens_per_request, 95pct_tokens)
  * tokens_per_dollar_breakdown.csv (showing cost by model variant and cache profile)
  * latency_vs_cost.csv (p50/p95 latency vs cost curve for each batching window)

Acceptance criteria (proposed for MAP signoff):
- Unit-econ delta between quoted tokens/$ and measured tokens/$ within +/- 12% at your median traffic profile.
- p95 latency under the agreed SLO at the chosen batching profile.
- No model quality regression > 1.5% on your sample eval set when using q8 quantized variant; if exceeded, we recommend fallback and quantify cost impact.

Irene — I'll kick off the runs tonight and push partial outputs to the Drive. Amit — please confirm the ingest rates and whether you want additional session stickiness simulated (we assumed session affinity = true by default).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: simulation_command_list.sh (reference), notes included in unit-cost-simulation-notes.pdf

From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@novushealth.com>

Subject: Re: MAP: unitized cost-trace validation + evaluation plan (tokens/$, caching & batching)

Thanks everyone — that plan looks good. Two quick clarifications from our side before you run the full sweep: 

1) Ingest rates: please run baseline at 15 rps, then step to 50 rps and 150 rps (we want to see behavior under load spikes).
2) Session stickiness: yes, please simulate session affinity; roughly 70% of our traffic is multi-turn within a 10-minute window.

Amit and I are available for a 30-minute readout on Nov 23 at 11:00 PT; if you need more time for analysis, shift to Nov 24 and tell us a preferred 30–45 minute slot.

We appreciate the explicit artifacts (tokens_per_dollar_breakdown.csv and latency_vs_cost.csv) — those are exactly what finance will need to sign off.

Emma Taylor
Senior Product Manager, Novus Health
emma.taylor@novushealth.com
